title: Welcome home
situation: You are {{Markus}}, an android, caretaker and companion to {{Carl}}, the elderly painter whose paints you have just collected. It is November 5th, 2038, just before ten in the morning. The bus drops you in your neighborhood and you walk up to {{Carl}}’s house with the package. At the door: “Alarm deactivated. Welcome home, {{Markus}}.” The door opens by itself and you step inside. You set the package down on the hutch in the hall and hang up your coat. Your next task is to take care of {{Carl}}, who is still asleep upstairs.

situationWhen.text: In the hall mirror you see your shirt, torn where the protesters grabbed you.

facts: You came home to {{Carl}}’s house with his paints and left them on the hutch in the hall.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has delivered the package. The house is quiet; {{Carl}} is still asleep upstairs.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVING HOME and the next main-line node DROP OFF PACKAGE (the game’s objective DEPOSIT PACKAGE), narrated as one event. The alarm line is the template’s; the date and time (NOV 5TH, 2038, AM 09:58), the self-opening door, the hutch and the coat are the wiki transcript’s (“Markus places the package on hutch and hangs up his coat”). The mirror sentence appears only when the protesters tore his clothes in Shades of Color (`clothesTorn`), as the transcript’s mirror text changes (“his torn shirt” / “his unscathed shirt”). Left out: the optional looks at the mirror and at the painting behind the bench, which are not chart nodes. No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

title: The magazine in the living room
situation: You are {{Markus}}, in {{Carl}}’s house before waking him. On the table in front of the living-room television lies a magazine with two covers.

media.title: Century: The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It
facts: Century (cover: “Frozen treasures”; also “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) reports that Russia’s interest in the North Pole has intensified since precious minerals used in synthesizing thirium were found trapped in the ice; surplus reserves would let either the US or Russia build more advanced androids and greatly boost its military and industrial output. NATO says “A conflict would benefit nobody”; President {{Warren}}: “It’s simple. Russia has no business in the Arctic. If the Kremlin doesn’t understand that, we will make them understand.”

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today (cover: “Life Found on Titan!”; also “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”) reports that a probe launched nineteen years ago has confirmed microorganisms living hundreds of kilometers below Titan’s surface, in a salt-water ocean under thick ice; after similar finds on Enceladus, life may be common in the universe. NASA calls its android expedition to Io one of many voyages seeking extraterrestrial life, and {{CyberLife}} says its space-faring androids are specially designed for long-range missions of this kind.

adaptationNote: The chart’s optional side nodes READ “NORTH POLE RUSSIA” and READ “LIFE ON TITAN”: one magazine on the living-room table in front of the TV with two covers (the transcript’s “Read Magazine” with two tabs; BOOKWORM No. 2 and No. 27), drawn on the chart with no line to the main path. In the game it can be read from arrival until the pastime is chosen; here it is offered now, and whatever is left unread is offered again with the TV after breakfast (R05b). Facts are summarized from the article text in the transcript; interviewees are not named. No public-opinion effect: the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter, and the earlier version’s note that news can lower opinion is dropped. Titles corrected to the magazine’s own (“The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It”, “Life Found on Titan!”).

options.text: Open the cage and switch the two birds on before going upstairs.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} opens the cage, kneels, and switches on one bird with its button, then the other. They come alive and chirp at each other. He closes the cage and goes upstairs to wake {{Carl}}.

options.text: Leave the birds and go upstairs to wake {{Carl}}.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} goes upstairs to wake {{Carl}}.

In the game it can be done before or after waking Carl; here it is offered once, before going upstairs, with going straight up as the alternative. No stat change.

title: Waking {{Carl}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}. Upstairs, {{Carl}} is asleep in his bed, snoring. You draw the curtains; he wakes, shielding his eyes. “Good morning, {{Carl}}.” “Good morning.” “It’s 10 AM. The weather’s partly cloudy, 54°, 80% humidity, with a strong possibility of afternoon showers.” “It sounds like a good day to spend in bed…” “I did go to pick up the paint that you ordered.” “Oh yes, I’d forgotten! That is the difference between you and me, right {{Markus}}? You never forget anything…” You prepare the syringe with his medicine. “Show me your arm please, {{Carl}}.” “No!” “{{Carl}}…” He sighs and holds out his arm. “Thank you.” As you give the injection, he grumbles: “I just opened my eyes and I’m already gritting my teeth… Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly… All this effort to keep ’em going…”
facts: Every morning you give {{Carl}} his medicine by injection. He told you: “Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly… All this effort to keep ’em going…”
adaptationNote: The chart’s main-line node WAKE CARL (objectives WAKE CARL UPSTAIRS and ADMINISTER CARL’S MEDICINE). Every line is the template’s; the curtains, the syringe and Carl’s sigh are the transcript’s. Left out: the line “Our morning routine.”, marked cut in the template. No stat change: the template has no arrow anywhere in the chapter, and the wiki gives no relationship, public-opinion or instability change for it (Markus has no Carl relationship stat).

title: {{Carl}} notices your clothes
situation: You are {{Markus}}, finishing {{Carl}}’s injection. He looks at you, concerned, and gently touches your arm. “What happened to your clothes?” You answer: “Oh, it’s nothing… Just some demonstrators in the street, {{Carl}}…” “What a bunch of idiots… They think they can stop progress by roughing up a few androids? I hope they didn’t harm you…” “Oh, no, no… They just pushed me around, {{Carl}}. I’m fine.”
whenNot: Markus was not harassed by the protesters in Shades of Color, so his clothes are intact.
facts: {{Carl}} noticed your torn clothes and was worried for you; he called the protesters “a bunch of idiots” who think they can stop progress by roughing up androids. You told him it was nothing.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} finishes the injection and puts the syringe away.

title: Breakfast
situation: You are {{Markus}}. “Okay. I’ll take you to the bathroom now.” You carry {{Carl}} to the bathroom and run his bath, then settle him in his wheelchair and push him out along the balcony. “Anything special on the agenda today?” “Yes, there’s the opening of your retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art. The gallery director left four messages asking to confirm your attendance.” “I haven’t decided yet. We’ll see about that later.” “Okay.” “What else?” “Just your usual fan mail. I’ve already answered.” “Any news from {{Leo}}?” “No, {{Carl}}. I can call him if you like?” “No. No, don’t bother.” You take him down in the wheelchair elevator to the living room. “I’m starving.” “Well, your breakfast is ready. Bacon and eggs, just the way you like them.” “Thank you, {{Markus}}.” “You’re welcome.” You bring the tray from the kitchen and serve him at the dining table. “Thank you, {{Markus}}. Television.” The TV comes on with the news. You pour his coffee. “Why don’t you find something to do while I finish my breakfast?” “Sure… Okay, {{Carl}}.”
facts: {{Carl}}’s retrospective opens today at the Museum of Modern Art; the gallery director has left four messages asking him to confirm, and he has not decided whether to go.

title: {{Leo}}
situation: You are {{Markus}}. You open your eyes. {{Carl}} is staring at your canvas. “Oh my God…” A voice from the doorway: “Hey, Dad.” A young man has walked into the studio. “{{Leo}}… I didn’t hear you come in…” “Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I’d stop by… It’s been awhile, right?” “You all right? You don’t look so good.” “Oh, yeah, yeah, I’m fine… Hey listen, uh… I need some cash, Dad.” “Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?” “Uh well, it just goes, you know?” “Yeah… Yeah, you’re on it again, aren’t you?” “No, no, no, I swear it’s not that…” “Don’t lie to me, {{Leo}}.” “What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that’s all!” “Sorry… the answer’s no.” “What? Why?” “You know why.” “Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what’s it got that I don’t? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son. IT’S A FUCKING MACHINE!” He shoves you violently. “{{Leo}}, that’s enough! ENOUGH!” “You don’t care about anything except yourself and your goddamn paintings. You’ve never loved anyone. You’ve never loved me, Dad… You never loved me.” He storms out.
